messages:
Maria G: Quick sync from the Console arch retro — we have a noticeable tail hit on dashboard queries when authz is applied at the gateway. Need to pick an approach.
Raj P: Seen it too. Gateway-level filtering is attractive for early rejects but the cache key explosion is real.
Lee T: Measured numbers from yesterday's run: p50 +1ms, p95 +22ms, p99 +120ms for tenants with multiple roles.
Lee T: Cache hit rate for tiles dropped ~20% when we included role bits in cache key.
Oliver S: Gateway annotates permissions in headers -> downstream caches include them -> keys blow up. Also couples gateway to policy DSL.
Maria G: High-level options: (A) Keep gateway cheap and mark "possible partial"; full enforcement in query service with stable cache keys. (B) Let query surface own authz and bake coarse-grained permission buckets into cache keys.
Raj P: Option A keeps console code simpler but you push variability into caches. Option B centralizes logic but needs a good bucket strategy.
Lee T: I'm leaning hybrid: gateway does a fast tenant-level allow/deny and sets a short header `x-authz-status: allow|deny|partial`. Query service then does the final eval and decides a cache bucket id.
Oliver S: I like the hybrid. It reduces wasted execution for rejects and keeps cache bucketing responsibility where we can control it.
Lee T: Sketch of the bucketizer flow: ```
policy = get_policy(tenant)
bucket = bucketize(policy) // coarse stable id
key = f"dash:{tenant}:{view}:{bucket}"
```
Maria G: Important: bucketizer needs to be stable across small rule tweaks. We should version buckets and only change id when a policy crosses a meaningful threshold.
Raj P: Agree. Also need fallback: if a request's policy doesn't match the cache bucket (stale), fall back to full-eval and mark metric.
Lee T: Spike plan: 1) Implement bucketizer prototype + counters (churn, misses) in a canary binary (2d). 2) Run load scenario with multi-role tenants (1d). 3) If hit rate > 85% in canary, opt-in rollout per customer.
Oliver S: Add `x-cache-bucket` internal header so edge/infra caches can key on it. For Dedicated/Private customers make it toggleable.
Raj P: Threats: coarse authz exposure via headers -> must be internal-only, TLS-only, and masked by sidecars/logging rules. I'll help write the threat model.
Maria G: Ops asks: dashboard for per-tenant bucket churn, miss-rate, and an alert if churn >10% over 1h. Also surface the fraction of requests served from bucketed cache vs full-eval.
Oliver S: Long-term: move bucketizer into the query service as a policy translation module that outputs enforcement predicates + cache bucket mapping. Keeps gateway decoupled.
Lee T: Implementation notes: make bucketizer deterministic across languages (proto encoding + stable hashing). Add a version field to the bucket id: `v2-<hash>`.
Maria G: Can we avoid changing public telemetry? Keep metrics internal and mark bucket header as internal only.
Raj P: Also add masking rules to Fluentd/sidecar to strip `x-cache-bucket` from logs.
infra-bot: Load test artifacts uploaded: https://artifacts.redwoodinternal.local/console-bucket-spike/1755550000
Maria G: Next steps: Lee + Oliver spike this week, Raj helps with threat model and logging masks, I'll draft a short RFC with the hybrid approach and the bucketizer design. Meeting tomorrow 10:30 for anyone who wants to join. :thumbsup:
